study_id: Kampaktsis et al. - 2021 - State-of-the-art machine learning algorithms for the prediction of outcomes after contemporary heart

eligibility.Eligibility Rationale: The article analyzes adult heart transplant recipients using non‑linear machine learning models to predict post‑transplant survival, compares against standard risk scores, and is a peer‑reviewed publication from 2021.

identification_methods.Comments: Retrospective analysis of UNOS registry data focusing on adult heart transplantation outcomes.
identification_methods.Institution: Division of Cardiology, New York University Langone Medical Center, New York, USA
identification_methods.Address: 5501 St Avenue, New York, NY 10021, USA
identification_methods.Dataset Source: United Network for Organ Sharing (UNOS) database
identification_methods.Identification Notes: Included adult heart transplant recipients (≥18 years) from UNOS between 2010‑2018; excluded multiple transplants, non‑adults, patients with <1‑year follow‑up, and variables with >10% missing values.
identification_methods.Design: Retrospective cohort study using registry data
identification_methods.AI Model Architecture: Adaboost, Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Support Vector Machine, K‑nearest neighbor
identification_methods.Class Imbalance: Random oversampling applied to balance outcome classes in training set
identification_methods.Input Variables: Pre‑transplant variables (134 total, 39 selected by feature selection) including recipient and donor demographics, clinical and laboratory data
identification_methods.Missing Data Handling: Variables with >10% missing values were excluded; no imputation performed
identification_methods.Validation Method: Random split of dataset into derivation (75%) and validation (25%) cohorts; internal validation on held‑out cohort
identification_methods.Methods Notes: Feature selection using SVM-FuzCoC; hyperparameter optimization for each model; LIME used for explainability; performance assessed by AUC, sensitivity, specificity.

population.Inclusion criteria: Adult heart transplant recipients from the UNOS database between 2010 and 2018
population.Exclusion criteria: Patients with multiple transplants during the index hospitalization, non-adult patients, and patients with less than 1-year follow-up; variables with >10% missing values were not analyzed
population.Population Notes: Cohort randomly split into derivation (75%, n=13,969) and validation (25%, n=4,656) cohorts; oversampling applied to balance outcome groups

interventions_outcomes.Specific Algorithm Name: Adaboost, Support Vector Machine, Decision Tree, K-nearest neighbor, Logistic Regression
interventions_outcomes.Intervention Input Data Modality: Pre-transplant clinical variables (recipient and donor characteristics) in tabular format
interventions_outcomes.Interventions Notes: Random oversampling to balance classes; hyperparameter optimization applied to each model
interventions_outcomes.Outcomes Notes: Primary outcome is 1‑year mortality after heart transplantation
interventions_outcomes.Result data Notes: AUC values reported for each ML model and for IMPACT score; best performance by Adaboost
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome group: All adult heart transplant recipients in the validation cohort
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Metric Definition: AUC on the held‑out validation cohort
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Notes: Best performing model was Adaboost with AUC 0.689
